newsitem.title: USA: USDA "grossly exaggerated" CRP benefit - Grain group.
newsitem.headline: USDA "grossly exaggerated" CRP benefit - Grain group.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department "grossly exaggerated" the amount of highly erodible land accepted into the Conservation Reserve in May, a grain industry group said Monday.

In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, the National Grain and Feed Association questioned USDA's definition of highly erodible land and said " the assertion that there is anything near 84 percent of CRP land that is highly erodible should be corrected for the public record and an accurate assessment given."

USDA's decision to enroll a total of 3.22 million acres in Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota put the United States in the "politically embarrassing position of importing selected classes of wheat from Canada -- hard red spring and durum," the letter said.

Park Shackleford, one of the USDA officials who supervised the May enrollment, said USDA applied the same definition of highly erodible land was used for CRP and "conservation compliance" rules that require anti-erosion tillage practices.
The USDA definition is land with an erodibility index of at least eight on one-third of the acreage. NGFA cited criteria that with care land with far higher ratings could be tilled.
